record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: Can every set of n points in a rectangle of dimensions sqrt(3) by n−1 be connected by a set of length at most sqrt(3)(n−1)+o(1)?

evidence.quote: Question 2.11. Is it true that one can always connect n points in a rectangle √3×(n−1) by a set of length at most √3(n−1)+o(1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be a positive integer and consider any set $S$ of $n$ points contained in a closed planar rectangle of dimensions $\sqrt{3} \times (n-1)$. A connecting set for $S$ is any connected subset $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (for instance a Steiner tree or, more generally, a connected set of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) such that $S \subset \Sigma$; its length is the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$.

Determine whether the following holds: there exists a function $\varepsilon(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$ and every choice of $n$ points in a $\sqrt{3} \times (n-1)$ rectangle, the points can be connected by a connected planar set of length at most
$$\sqrt{3}\,(n-1) + \varepsilon(n).$$

Equivalently, is it true that the worst-case minimum length needed to connect $n$ points lying in a $\sqrt{3} \times (n-1)$ rectangle is $\sqrt{3}(n-1) + o(1)$ as $n \to \infty$?
